source.title: Mapping Sub-Second Structure in Mouse Behavior

confidence_rationale: This is the foundational paper for Motion Sequencing (MoSeq), a formal, rigorous, widely-adopted generative-model approach to exactly the 'discovery-oriented analysis' the source thought gestures at informally. It demonstrates that a real, established, statistically principled method exists for decomposing continuous behavior into a reusable vocabulary of stereotyped modules with defined transition probabilities -- direct confirmation that the thought's aspiration (motifs/states/transitions rather than aggregate totals) is not merely plausible but already has a mature methodological answer in computational ethology. Confidence held at 0.7 rather than higher because REE's environment (2D/discrete grid navigation) differs substantially from MoSeq's domain (3D depth-video pose dynamics in an open field), so the specific modeling machinery would need substantial adaptation, not direct reuse.
failure_signatures: MoSeq's own methodology requires selecting a model-order hyperparameter (the number of distinct behavioral syllables/states), which has no single objectively correct value -- illustrating that even a rigorous, formal, unsupervised discovery method does not eliminate researcher degrees of freedom, it relocates them from ad hoc metric choice to model-order/hyperparameter choice, a caution directly relevant to how GOV-BEHADJ-1's 'Discover' step would need its own explicit anti-Goodharting safeguards if implemented with an analogous generative model.

mapping.source_claim_statement: 3D depth-camera imaging of freely moving mice, combined with an autoregressive hidden Markov model (AR-HMM) over pose dynamics, shows that mouse behavior is organized into sub-second (~300ms), reused, stereotyped modules ('syllables') with well-defined transition probabilities between them -- a formal, generative-model-based decomposition of continuous behavior into discrete, statistically discoverable units, without pre-specifying which behaviors to look for.
mapping.ree_translation: This is a mature, working instantiation of exactly the source thought's 'behaviour as structured process, not merely aggregate output' section and its 'discovery-oriented' analytical channel. If GOV-BEHADJ-1 is ever hardened into a skill, the 'Discover' step should point to this class of method (formal generative segmentation with an explicit transition-probability structure) as the rigorous baseline, rather than informal visual inspection or ad hoc post-hoc feature engineering -- the source thought's own phrasing ('what behavioural structure is present that we did not think to measure?') is precisely the question MoSeq-class methods are built to answer with statistical rigor.
mapping.mapping_caveat: MoSeq operates on continuous, high-dimensional 3D pose data from a physical animal in an open field; REE's Fishtank agent operates in a discrete or low-dimensional grid environment with a much smaller and more constrained action/state space. A direct AR-HMM-over-pose adaptation is not appropriate; the transferable content is the modeling PHILOSOPHY (formal generative segmentation over informal metric engineering) and the general architecture (discrete latent states + explicit transition structure), not the specific depth-video pipeline.
mapping.source_context: Freely moving C57BL/6J mice in an open field, 3D depth camera imaging, unsupervised AR-HMM segmentation of continuous pose-dynamics time series into discrete behavioral modules.

confidence_components.notes: Foundational, highly-cited NeuroResource paper in a top neuroscience journal, methodologically rigorous and since extensively validated and extended (MoSeq2, keypoint-MoSeq). Mapping fidelity moderate: REE's environment and observation modality differ substantially from MoSeq's, so the specific technique would need reinvention, but the underlying discovery-oriented modeling philosophy transfers well.
